content: The following are the steps to properly don personal protective equipment (PPE), including a coverall, as outlined by the World Health Organization (WHO). The responsibility for interpreting and using the information lies with the reader. 1. Begin by removing all personal items, such as jewelry, watches, cell phones, and pens, to avoid contamination. 2. Proceed to the clean area located at the entrance of the isolation unit. 3. Conduct a visual inspection to confirm that all PPE components are available in the correct sizes and are of appropriate quality. 4. Perform the process of donning PPE under the guidance and supervision of a trained observer or colleague. 5. In the changing room, put on a scrub suit and rubber boots. If rubber boots are unavailable, wear closed shoes (preferably slip-ons without shoelaces) that fully cover the dorsum of the foot and ankles, along with non-slip, impermeable shoe covers. 6. Put on the coverall, ensuring it fits properly and provides full coverage. 7. Wear a face shield or goggles to protect the eyes. 8. Cover the head and neck using a surgical bonnet that extends to cover the neck and sides of the head. Alternatively, use a hood, preferably in combination with a face shield. 9. Avoid using adhesive tape to secure gloves. Some coverall designs include built-in finger loops for this purpose.
